text.p: German diversified industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG said on Wednesday it planned to merge its two main plant construction units, Lurgi and Lentjes under the Lurgi AG name.

The group said in a statement the new Lurgi group would be headed by current Lentjes management board chairman, Heinrich-Werner Mathes. Steps would be taken in the coming weeks to begin the merger process, it said.
MG said the merger, effective October 1, would achieve better coordination between the two units and better exploit synergies between their activities.
Lurgi would be responsible for five units: Lurgi Metallurgie GmbH, Lurgi Umwelt GmbH, Lurgi OelGas Chemie GmbH, Zimmer AG and Lentjes AG.
The new unit would have sales of four billion marks, it said and employ about 6,200 people.

MG management board chairman Kajo Neukirchen said the move marked a further stage in the revamping of Metallgesellschaft which began after the company ran into billions of marks of debt on risky oil deals in the United States.
"In the first phase we restructured MG and brought it back to financial health. In the second phase we will optimise the company," he said.
He added that the restructuring in plant construction was an example of this type of optimisation and said that similar moves would also be made in other areas.
All such moves would be aimed at increasing shareholder value, he said.
A spokesman for the company said that the merger should not involve the loss of many jobs and said there were no plans to list the unit in the near future.

Lurgi -- which made a pre-tax profit of 113 million marks ($76 million) in the 1994/95 business year ended September 30 -- is one of the most profitable sections of MG. The spokesman said Lurgi would this year report the best profit in its 99-year history.
Lentjes is also expected to report a good profit for 1995/96 compared with 28 million marks in 1994/95, he added. ($1=1.4791 Mark)
